instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: The ground for boasting: "I would rather die than have anyone deprive me of my ground for boasting. For if I preach the gospel, that gives me no ground for boasting. For necessity is laid upon me" (1Co 9:15–16); The preaching itself is no ground, because it is laid on him. The ground is that he preached "free of charge" (9:18).

Paul's most frequent boast is in other people: "I have great pride in you; I am filled with comfort. In all our affliction, I am overflowing with joy" (2Co 7:4); His boasts to Titus about them "proved true" (7:14). He asks them to "give proof ... of our boasting about you" (8:24). He sends brothers "so that our boasting about you may not prove empty" (9:3), or "we would be humiliated" (9:4). The boast puts Paul's own standing at risk on the conduct of others; "your readiness, of which I boast about you ... your zeal has stirred up most of them" (9:2); At Christ's coming; "what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at his coming? Is it not you?" (1Th 2:19); "on the day of our Lord Jesus you will boast of us as we will boast of you" (2Co 1:14); "so that in the day of Christ I may be proud that I did not run in vain" (Php 2:16); "we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God for your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions" (2Th 1:4); "so that in me you may have ample cause to glory in Christ Jesus" (Php 1:26); His work, which is Christ's. "I have reason to be proud of my work for God. For I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me" (Rom 15:17–18). The pride is in a work he credits to Christ; "by my pride in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die every day!" (1Co 15:31); "Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation, and the rich in his humiliation" (Jam 1:9–10, carried).

Are any of the pride words indicative of God's characteristics? Yes: The gāʾôn family is used of God's majesty: "majesty", "triumphed gloriously", "robed in majesty" (Exo 15:1, 7; Psa 93:1; Isa 2:10); "Majesty" is used as a name for God (Heb 1:3; 8:1); The mocking words are used of God's derision: "He who sits in the heavens laughs" (Psa 2:4); "Toward the scorners he is scornful" (Pro 3:34); God is never the subject of a boast in these verses. He is its right object: "let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me" (Jer 9:24).

Refinement 2: the same words for people are not always pride: God gives a "pride" or majesty to his people: chosen (Psa 47:4), given (Isa 4:2), made (Isa 60:15), restored (Nah 2:2); A heart can be "courageous [lifted up] in the ways of the Lord" (2Ch 17:6); The boast can be moved to God (1Co 1:31; Rom 5:2–3, 11); The measure assigned by God is the right measure (Rom 12:3; 2Co 10:13); I read: the verses draw the line by source and direction, not by the word. There is height that is one's own by nature (God), height given by God (his people, in his ways), and height taken, held against the giver, or set over others (pride).

This is where the change-of-character reading (#1919) would start. No reading has been done: H1347 gāʾôn: human "pride" (25) versus God's "majesty" (9) versus "the thicket of the Jordan" (3); H1361 gābah: "proud" and "haughty" (Eze 28:2, 5; 2Ch 26:16; 32:25) versus "towered" and "higher" (physical) versus "exalted" of God (Isa 5:16) and of the servant (Isa 52:13); H1364 gābōah and H1363 gōbah: high walls and tall men versus "haughty eyes" and "a haughty spirit" (Pro 16:18); G2744 kauchaomai: "boast" versus "rejoice" (Rom 5:2–3, 11). Boasting in oneself versus "let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord" (1Co 1:31; 2Co 10:17); H1984H hālal: "boast" versus "glory" and "exult" (Jer 9:24, "let him who boasts boast in this"); G1702 empaizō: Jesus "mocked" in the passion accounts versus Herod "tricked" by the magi (Mat 2:16); H7292 rāhab: "insolent" (Isa 3:5) versus "plead urgently" (Pro 6:3) versus "overwhelm" (Song 6:5).
No verse makes God the subject of a boast. He is the one boasted in (Jer 9:24).

Pride is the given held as one's own: "What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?" (1Co 4:7); In story, each time:; "when he was strong, he grew proud" (2Ch 26:16); "did not make return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was proud" (2Ch 32:25); "when his heart was lifted up" (Dan 5:20); "your heart has become proud in your wealth" (Eze 28:5); "its heart was proud of its height" (Eze 31:10); In the law it is foreseen: "your heart be lifted up, and you forget the Lord your God ... Beware lest you say in your heart, 'My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth'" (Deu 8:14, 17); It credits its own hand. "By the strength of my hand I have done it", said by the one who was the Lord's rod: "Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it" (Isa 10:13, 15). And "which I have built by my mighty power" (Dan 4:30); I read: the line the verses draw is not between having height and having none. It is the source and the direction. Height that is one's own by nature belongs to God alone. Height that is given is held from him. Pride is the given taken as one's own, and turned against the giver or over others. This is the researcher's "assumed position", in the verses' own words.

The boast is pride said aloud: In self: "Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom" (Jer 9:23); About tomorrow: "Do not boast about tomorrow" (Pro 27:1); "you boast in your arrogance" (Jam 4:16); Of a gift not given (Pro 25:14).

The humble hear what God did for another, and are glad: "My soul makes its boast in the Lord; let the humble hear and be glad" (Psa 34:2). David's own deliverance follows: "I sought the Lord, and he answered me" (34:4). The superscription sets it after "he changed his behavior before Abimelech"; "When the humble see it they will be glad" (Psa 69:32). "It" is the deliverance of the speaker, who has said "I am afflicted and in pain" (69:29); I read: in both psalms, one man's boast is in the Lord, not in himself, and the humble are those who are glad at it. Their gladness is at what God did for someone else.

In wisdom: "show his works in the meekness of wisdom. But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast" (Jam 3:13–14). Meekness is the mark of true wisdom. Selfish ambition in the heart is its counterfeit, as in Phili 2:3 (group III).

A reversal, and a boast turned around: "Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation, and the rich in his humiliation, because like a flower of the grass he will pass away" (Jam 1:9–10); "God chose what is low and despised in the world, even things that are not, to bring to nothing things that are, so that no human being might boast in the presence of God … 'Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord'" (1Cor 1:28–31); I read: in both, the low is where God's choosing and lifting are seen. The boast is moved from what one has to what God does. The rich man's "humiliation" is something to boast in, because it tells him the truth: he passes like grass.

Luk 10:17, 20: "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!", and Jesus: "Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.": The subjection of spirits is real, and "in your name"; The joy is moved from the power that subjects to the gift received; I read: this is the same turn as Jam 1:9–10 and 1Cor 1:31 (batch 4): the boast or the joy moved from what one does to what God gives; The passage goes on: Jesus thanks the Father for revealing these things "to little children" (10:21); Cited in 10.1, Ch 11 and 13.3.
2.3 The soul and wickedness: "The soul of the wicked desires evil" (Pro 21:10); "their soul delights in their abominations" (Isa 66:3); "the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul" (Psa 10:3)

4.5 Wind and vanity — falsehood as insubstantial (see R9): "Ephraim feeds on the wind … they multiply falsehood" (Hos 12:1).; "Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give" (Pro 25:14).

9.4 Flesh, boasting and the Spirit (NT): "so that no human being [*flesh*] might boast in the presence of God" (1Co 1:29); "Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast" (2Co 11:18); "that they may boast in your flesh" (Gal 6:13); "we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh" (Phili 3:3) [D1]; "the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life" (1Jo 2:16); "speaking loud boasts of folly, they entice by sensual passions of the flesh" (2Pe 2:18); "puffed up without reason by his sensuous [*fleshly*] mind" (Col 2:18)
Conscience as the proper boast: "our boast is this, the testimony of our conscience" (2Co 1:12).

5.5 ◆ Fringe (M74): "guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms [*bosom*]" (Mic 7:5) — the closest intimacy as the place for guarding; The Gerasene: "He was kept under guard and bound with chains … but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon" (Luk 8:29) [O] — human guarding fails against the spirit; the word of Jesus succeeds (8:29a); "who sit in tombs, and spend the night in secret places [*nāṣar*] … eat pig's flesh" (Isa 65:4); "they desire to have you circumcised that they may boast in your flesh" (Gal 6:13); "guard the good deposit … by the Holy Spirit who dwells within us" (2Ti 1:14) [D1]; "maintain the unity of the Spirit" (Eph 4:3) [D2]; "I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey" (Eze 36:27) [D1] — the carefulness is caused by the Spirit

1.10 Evil desire of the soul: "the great man utters the evil desire of his soul" (Mic 7:3); "The soul of the wicked desires evil" (Pro 21:10); "the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul, and the one greedy for gain … renounces the Lord" (Psa 10:3); "These have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations" (Isa 66:3); "The Lord … thwarts the craving [*nephesh*] of the wicked" (Pro 10:3); "The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing" (Pro 13:4)

What he delights in: "steadfast love, justice, and righteousness" (Jer 9:24). The verse before forbids boasting in wisdom, might and riches. The one who may boast boasts "that he understands and knows me". "His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man" (Psa 147:10), beside "those who fear him" (147:11, already in 10.9). Strength is turned down twice, once as a boast and once as a delight.

Knowing it.: *"If anyone's will is to do God's will, he will know whether the teaching is from God"* (Joh 7:17). The willing comes first, and the knowing follows it.; Paul was *"appointed … to know his will"* (Act 22:14), and was told the next moment *"why do you wait?"* (22:16).; *"Do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is"* (Eph 5:17), with *"be filled with the Spirit"* (5:18).; Knowing can stand without doing: *"you … know his will and approve what is excellent"* (Rom 2:18), said to one who *"boast[s] in God"* (2:17) and teaches others (2:19–21).; The servant *"who knew his master's will but did not get ready or act according to his will"* is beaten more than the one who did not know (Luk 12:47–48).

11. Zeal passed on (Ch 11 §6): *"I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the people of Macedonia … And your zeal has stirred up most of them"* (2Co 9:2). The zeal of one church stirs another. The stirring verb is the one used of fathers provoking children (Col 3:21; anger ledger AG-239). Here it is aimed at good.

Jealousy among the wise (Jam 3:14–16). *"But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast and be false to the truth. This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic. For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every vile practice."*: It is set against *"Who is wise and understanding among you?"* (3:13). So it is the jealousy of people who would be counted wise.; "Bitter" is a taste. Psalm 73 has "embittered" too.; It is "in your hearts", and it shows outwardly as "disorder".; James names its source in three words. The middle one, "unspiritual", is literally "soulish".

It opens with a superlative, that Paul's most frequent boast is in other people. In this subgroup more of Paul's boasts are of himself, his authority, his measure or his weakness (2Cor 10:8-16, 11:10-30, 12:1-9, Gal 6:14, 1Cor 9:15-16, 2Cor 1:12) than of other people (2Cor 7:14, 8:24, 9:2-3, 2Th 1:4, 1Th 2:19, 2Cor 1:14); the superlative was not checked and does not hold (B:36).

actions.new_text: Paul often boasts in other people: his pride in the Corinthians (2Co 7:4); his boasts to Titus that proved true (7:14); the proof of his boasting he asks of them (8:24); the brothers sent so the boast is not empty or he humiliated (9:3-4); their readiness and zeal (9:2); the Thessalonians as his crown of boasting at Christ's coming (1Th 2:19); the mutual boast on the day of the Lord (2Co 1:14); his boast in their steadfastness (2Th 1:4). His own standing rests on their conduct (2Co 9:4).
actions.checked: 2Cor 7:4, 7:14, 8:24, 9:2-4, 1:14, 1Th 2:19, 2Th 1:4 in the verse table; Paul's other boasts in this subgroup counted against them (2Cor 10:8-16, 11:10-30, 12:1-9, Gal 6:14, 1Cor 9:15-16, 2Cor 1:12).
actions.reason: The superlative most frequent does not hold on count; restated without it.

The facts it lists (renderings that diverge for H1347, H1361, H1364, H1363, G2744, H1984H and others) are true of the verses named, but it opens with a process note (where a reading of #1919 would start, no reading done) that is stale and not evidence.

actions.new_text: Several codes of height and boasting carry opposite renderings: H1347 is human pride but God's majesty and the thicket of the Jordan; H1361 is proud and haughty (Eze 28:2, 5; 2Ch 26:16; 32:25) but also exalted of God (Isa 5:16) and of the servant (Isa 52:13); H1364 and H1363 are high walls and tall men but haughty eyes and spirit (Pro 16:18); G2744 is boast but also rejoice (Rom 5:2-3, 11), and boast in the Lord (1Co 1:31; 2Co 10:17); H1984H is boast but also glory (Jer 9:24).
actions.checked: The verses named in the verse table; the meaning ranges of H1347, H1361, H1364, H1363, G2744 and H1984H.
actions.reason: The stale process note is removed; the evidence of divergent renderings stays.

actions.checked: The subjects of every boast occurrence of the subgroup boasting (S1 readings 23631 to 23682): human beings, nations, the tongue, the axe; none is God.
actions.reason: The universal claim is limited to the verses actually read.
